title: Opal Legal - Contract Review Onboarding & Acceptance Pack
content:
Purpose:
This pack defines the evaluation, acceptance criteria, pinned prompts, and regression plan for onboarding the Opal Legal contract-review workload into Redwood. The goal is a production-ready contract redlining and clause-extraction endpoint that meets legal accuracy, low-hallucination, and latency targets while using Opal's private contract corpus (legal-priv-opa1).

Scope & Contact
- Customer: Opal Legal (contract_review product)
- Redwood owner: Maya Chen (Applied ML)
- Customer technical contact: Priya Nair (Opal Legal, Eng Lead)
- Solutions engineering: Marco Alvarez

High-level tasks in this pack:
1) Pin a core prompt set for contract redline, summary, and clause extraction.
2) Define private dataset inventory, labeling schema, and access controls.
3) Specify quantitative acceptance thresholds and manual QA processes.
4) Provide regression gate and continuous monitoring plan.
5) Signoff checklist and required approvers.

Pinned prompts (locked for initial rollout)
- Redline Prompt (for suggested edits):
  "You are a contract analyst. For the following contract excerpt, list risky clauses, propose precise replacement language, and explain reasoning in 2-3 sentences per item. Return JSON with keys: issues (array of {clause_id, issue_type, suggested_text, rationale}). For any uncertain items, set confidence <=0.6."

- Summary Prompt (contract-level TL;DR):
  "Produce a 5-line executive summary of the contract, highlighting term length, auto-renewals, termination rights, indemnities, and any unusual payment conditions. State relevant clause locations (e.g., section 4.2)."

- Clause Extraction Prompt (structured extraction):
  "Extract the following fields into a table: effective_date, term_months, auto_renewal (boolean), termination_notice_days, liquidated_damages_clause (boolean), governing_law. Provide source span offsets and clause ids."

- Clarification/Follow-up Prompt (multi-turn support):
  "If the user asks a follow-up about a returned item, answer concisely with references to the original clause and use conservative language (do not invent facts). If information is missing, ask for the clause text."

Dataset inventory (private datasets)
- legal-priv-opa1 (primary training/holdout): 38,400 contract documents (NDAs, MSAs, SOWs). Label types: clause spans, extraction keys, redline annotations. Accessible only to eng-applied-ml team and Opal contract reviewers via gate 'access-group:opal-legal-ml'. PII notes: contains names, addresses; treated as sensitive.
- nda-samples-2023 (evaluation subset): 1,200 NDA pairs annotated with risk labels and redline examples. Read-only for evaluation harness.
- court-summary-deriv (external but customer-licensed): 4,300 entries used only for summary robustness tests.

Label schema (summary)
- clause_id: unique id
- clause_type: [payment, indemnity, termination, confidentiality, liability, IP, data-protection, other]
- risk_label: [low, medium, high] (annotator guidance included in Confluence)
- suggested_text: short replacement paragraph

Baseline & candidate models
- Baseline (customer currently using): redwood-legal-1.0 (quantized, tuned)
- Candidate (onboarding target): redwood-legal-2.1 / open-llama-3-70b-quantized (actual candidate commits linked in repo)

Evaluation metrics and acceptance thresholds
1) Clause Extraction (structured):
   - Metric: span-level F1 (micro) for clause boundaries and clause_type accuracy.
   - Acceptance: F1 >= 0.88 and clause_type accuracy >= 0.91 on nda-samples-2023 holdout.
2) Redline Suggestion (precision/quality):
   - Metric: human-annotator precision @ top-3 suggestions (manual eval) and a composite Quality Score (0-100) from 3 annotators.
   - Acceptance: Precision@3 >= 0.82 and mean Quality Score >= 78.
3) Summary Quality:
   - Metric: ROUGE-L + targeted factuality checks (entity/date match).
   - Acceptance: ROUGE-L >= 0.52 AND factuality pass-rate >= 97% (no introduced dates/amounts).
4) Hallucination & Safety:
   - Metric: hallucination rate measured via 500 random manual probes (claims not grounded in source).
   - Acceptance: hallucination rate < 3%. Any hallucination >0.3% on high-risk clauses triggers immediate rollback.
5) Latency & Throughput:
   - Metric: P95 latency for a 4k-token request under steady-state (1x concurrency) measured on Dedicated environment.
   - Acceptance: P95 <= 450ms; P99 <= 950ms.
6) Token cost estimate:
   - Metric: tokens per document and cost-per-1000-docs compared to baseline.
   - Constraint: total per-1000-doc inference cost must not exceed baseline by more than 12% unless quality delta justifies it.

Automatic evaluation harness
- Repo: github:repo/redwood/opal-legal-eval-harness (see linked PR for scripts).
- Scripts: run_eval.sh accepts model_id, dataset_id, seed. Output: CSV with metrics and saved artifacts (predictions, diffs).
- Dataset access: request via internal ACL flow; dataset ids used by harness are: legal-priv-opa1:holdout_v2, nda-samples-2023:test_v1.

Manual QA protocol
- 3 annotators per item, blind labeling. Dispute resolution by senior legal annotator.
- For redline suggestions: sample of 300 suggestions stratified by clause_type and risk_label.
- For summary factuality: 200 sampled contracts checked for dates, amounts, and governing law matches.

Regression gating rules (pre-deploy)
- A candidate model must pass all quantitative acceptance thresholds above.
- No metric may regress by >2% absolute vs baseline on critical metrics (clause F1, hallucination).
- If candidate shows improved quality but higher cost, product + customer must approve in writing.
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback if any of these triggers occur in canary windows:
   * Error rate spike > 1.5x baseline
   * Latency P95 increase > 30%
   * Hallucination alert (manual queue) > threshold

Monitoring & continuous checks (post-deploy)
- Production monitors: per-route Quality Alerts (sampled predictions flagged for manual review), latency SLOs, token-cost burn rate, and per-customer error budgets.
- Weekly regression snapshot: run full eval harness against legal-priv-opa1:holdout_v2 and check metric deltas.
- Monthly drift check: OOD rate measured by distance to training distribution using embedding-based detector.

Security & data handling
- Model request logs: redact full contract text in logs; store only metadata (document_id, clause_ids, token_count) in clear. Full-text logs encrypted with KMS key: projects/redwood/keys/opal-legal.
- Access: only eng-applied-ml, eng-infra for deployment, and Opal reviewers may access evaluation outputs via secure workspace.
- Privacy note: any failed manual QA annotations with PII must follow Opal's data retention policy; sample retention set to 90 days unless otherwise requested.

Edge cases & known limitations
- Complex amendments with inline change markers: model may under-segment clauses (known failure mode). Add a preprocessing rule to expand inline bullets into numbered sections for the evaluator.
- Non-English contracts: Out of scope for initial rollout.

Sign-off checklist (required approvers before dedicated rollout)
- [ ] Applied ML lead (Maya Chen) - verifies metric pass and regression logs.
- [ ] Solutions Engineering (Marco Alvarez) - approves latency/cost plan.
- [ ] Customer Security (Sofia Martinez) - approves data gating/KMS setup.
- [ ] Opal Legal product owner (Priya Nair) - business acceptance and manual QA signoff.
- [ ] Release engineering (release tag) - deployment runbook verified.

Post-signoff rollout plan
- Dry-run (internal only) for 72h against subset of traffic; monitor alerts.
- Customer can opt into two-phase rollout (redline-only, then summary/extraction).

Open questions / action items
- Confirm retention window for manual QA artifacts with Opal security (ASSIGNED: Sofia).
- Finalize cost parity threshold if candidate model improves Quality Score by >6% (ASSIGNED: Marco).
- Add interpreter test for amendment-style contracts (ASSIGNED: Ethan).

Appendix: sample test prompts (from anchored test suite)
1) "Section 7.3: The Contractor shall indemnify..." -> expect: flag indemnity missing carve-outs, suggested tightened text.
2) "Effective date appears as 'on the date of last signature'" -> expect: extraction: effective_date: null, follow-up prompt asking for signature dates.
3) Short NDA with non-compete clause -> expect: classification: confidentiality=true, non_compete=false, risk_label=medium.

Notes and references
- See Confluence onboarding guide for annotator instructions (linked_artifacts).
- Evaluation harness implements reproducible seeds for manual QA queues.

Summary
This pack is the single source of truth for Opal Legal onboarding. It locks the initial prompt set, defines private dataset use and access, formalizes acceptance thresholds emphasizing factuality and low hallucination, and prescribes a conservative, monitored rollout path with clear signoff responsibilities.
